rule: Articles and adjectives must match the noun's gender: el libro rojo, la casa roja. Most nouns ending in -o are masculine; most ending in -a are feminine, with well-known exceptions (el día, la mano, el problema).

examples.es: La mesa blanca está en la cocina.
examples.en: The white table is in the kitchen.
examples.note: mesa is feminine, so la and blanca.
A mixed or all-male group takes masculine plural.

common_mistake: English has no gender, so learners often freeze the adjective (rojo for everything) or guess from the English word instead of the Spanish noun.
